---
title: "Notes engine on a server"
description: "Run your notes' R sessions on a bigger server while OmicsBase stays on your machine."
---

A local installation runs your notes' R sessions on the machine it is installed on. To use a bigger machine, start the notes engine on a server and point your installation at it with `ENGINE_URL`.

Your installation connects to the server, and the server never connects back, so the installation can stay on a laptop behind a home router.

This moves notes only. To run Reports on another machine, see [Reports on your own computer](../start/reports-own-computer.qmd).

## What you need {#requirements}

- A working OmicsBase installation. See [Install on your own machine](install.qmd).
- A server with Docker and Compose v2.
- A DNS name pointing at the server, for example `engine.example.org`.
- Ports 80 and 443 open on the server, so it can get an HTTPS certificate and receive connections.

The engine must be reached at a public HTTPS address. An engine on a private address, such as a machine on your local network, is refused by OmicsBase.

## 1. Set up the server {#server}

On the server, download the three setup files into a new folder:

```bash
mkdir omicsbase-engine && cd omicsbase-engine
for f in docker-compose.yml Caddyfile .env.example; do
  curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xMuluh/omicsbase/main/local/engine-server/$f
done
cp .env.example .env
chmod 600 .env
```

## 2. Fill in the server's `.env` {#server-env}

Open `.env` on the server and set:

| Variable | Set it to |
| --- | --- |
| `ENGINE_DOMAIN` | The server's DNS name, for example `engine.example.org` |
| `OMICSBASE_ENGINE_SECRET` | The value of `OMICSBASE_ENGINE_SECRET` in `~/omicsbase/.env` on your installation |
| `OMICSBASE_VERSION` | The image version, `latest` by default. If you pinned a version on your installation, use the same one. |

Copy the secret from `~/omicsbase/.env`; the two must match.

## 3. Start the engine {#server-start}

On the server, in the `omicsbase-engine` folder:

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

This starts two containers: the engine, and Caddy in front of it. Caddy gets the HTTPS certificate for `ENGINE_DOMAIN` by itself.

## 4. Point OmicsBase at the server {#point-install}

On the machine where OmicsBase is installed, add this line to `~/omicsbase/.env`, with your server's name:

```text
ENGINE_URL=https://engine.example.org
```

Then restart OmicsBase:

```bash
cd ~/omicsbase && docker compose up -d
```

New notes now run on the server. Files of notes made before stay on the machine that ran them.

## The engine does not answer {#engine-does-not-answer}

**You see** in a note, while a cell runs:

```text
The notes engine is not answering. Still trying…
```

The cell keeps trying for about a minute. If the engine answers again, the cell carries on. If not, or if the engine cannot be reached when the cell starts, the cell ends with:

```text
Could not reach the notes engine at engine.example.org. Check that the server is running and that ENGINE_URL in ~/omicsbase/.env is right, then run the cell again.
```

OmicsBase also checks the engine once each time it starts. To see the result, run this on the machine where OmicsBase is installed:

```bash
cd ~/omicsbase && docker compose logs api | grep "notes engine"
```

It says either `The notes engine at engine.example.org answers.` or `The notes engine at engine.example.org does not answer:` followed by the reason.

To find the cause:

1. **Ask the engine yourself.** Open its health address, with your server's name, in a browser or with `curl`:

   ```bash
   curl https://engine.example.org/health
   ```

   A running engine answers `{"status":"ok"}`. The health address needs no secret and starts no R.

2. **If the health address does not answer,** check the server. In the `omicsbase-engine` folder:

   ```bash
   docker compose ps
   docker compose logs engine caddy
   ```

   Both containers must be running. Check also that the DNS name points at the server and that ports 80 and 443 are open.

3. **If the health address answers but cells still fail,** check `ENGINE_URL` in `~/omicsbase/.env` on your installation. It must be the same address, starting with `https://`. After a change, restart OmicsBase:

   ```bash
   cd ~/omicsbase && docker compose up -d
   ```

Then run the cell again.

## Where your data lives {#data}

With `ENGINE_URL` set, your notes' R sessions, files and plots live on the server, in the `omicsbase-engine` folder:

| Folder | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `data/projects/` | Files of notes: data, figures and results |
| `data/engine-cache/` | Downloaded ExperimentHub and AnnotationHub data |
| `data/caddy/` | Caddy's HTTPS certificate |

Your accounts and the notes' messages stay in `~/omicsbase/data/` on your machine.

## Security {#security}

- **The secret is the key to the server.** Anyone holding `OMICSBASE_ENGINE_SECRET` can run R on the engine. Keep `.env` private on both machines, and never share or commit it.
- **The server is on the internet.** Caddy publishes the engine on ports 80 and 443 of the server's name. The engine runs R only for requests that carry the secret; its health address answers without one.
- **One installation per secret.** Give the server the secret of the installation that uses it. If you think the secret has leaked, set a new value in `~/omicsbase/.env` (from `openssl rand -hex 32`), copy it to the server's `.env`, and run `docker compose up -d` on both.

## Update the server {#update}

On the server, in the `omicsbase-engine` folder:

```bash
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
```

Update the server when you update OmicsBase, so both run the same version. See [Updating and backups](updating.qmd).

## Go back to the engine on your machine {#go-back}

Remove the `ENGINE_URL` line from `~/omicsbase/.env`, or put `#` in front of it, then:

```bash
cd ~/omicsbase && docker compose up -d
```

New notes run on your machine again. Files of notes that ran on the server stay there.
